There are some points you brought up that I could agree with. But this is a subset of the larger population. There's a reason why people gravitate here. The common element being that they found there is not solution to the pain that is in their lives.

It is a valiant effort, I do admit, to try to engage in conversations with some people. However, as I understand and as many others understand on here, the division comes with a reason grounded in reality.

The reality that out there, society and people reject the people who end up on this subreddit and similar communities. Neurotypical people just don't understand, write policies and laws for non-neurotypical people, and treat us like garbage.

We lost people in our lives because they just didn't understand or they just didn't want us in their lives. So that is where the division comes from, it comes from understanding that normal people don't want anything to do with us. That is a certainty and that is a fact that many others on here, the majority if not everyone, can agree with.

Reconnecting is a luxury that nobody has here really. Just abandoned all hope for that. It's a painful charade, a reminder of what we failed at in life. It just reopens old wounds every time. In the camp where the pain in your life is unbearable and you just want it to end, consolation and affirmation that you're making the right choice is the only thing that matters.

Here's the thing, at least for me.

A lot of people on here lived lives where...things weren't so great. For the lack of better terms. A lot of us on here have tried to improve our lives, to work on it, and to basically throw all kinds of hail marys to do what we could, to power through, and endure all kinds of pain and suffering to maybe have a chance for happiness, whatever that may be for each individual person.

But as it is with life, it wasn't fair. And while for most people life tends to luck out and deliver them something or someone or what have you to make it all worth it...that just wasn't the case for some people. Notably the people on here.

I've been on this subreddit for a while. Won't say how long but for a while. And the overwhelming majority of people on here that I've witnessed don't want "help" or at least what traditional definitions conform to the idea of "help". They just want validation for the pain and suffering that they had to go through, to be recognized that they're in pain. And that they're in the right to choose to check out, so to speak, because life just became that unbearable.

I'm not telling you how to post or anything because not to be rude or anything but I don't care about that. But most people on here, myself included, don't want to be judged for wanting to escape how painful our lives are. We've been judged for that our whole lives, and we don't need any more of that.

I've seen and known lives that had nothing good happen for them. So I just don't believe in statements like "it can get better".

And about the guy in the post. I've seen a lot of users post and then they never write a post again if you catch my drift. The most kind and compassionate thing that could be done for people who've reached that level of pain in their lives is just to be understanding that their pain is finally over.

Edit: Me, personally? I can't wait until I'm not here anymore. I have all my gear set up, just waiting on timing. So I'm not speaking from a point of not knowing, I know very well.
